intent_text: Fix appCreate/appUpdate crash on null permissions input (#19571) * Fix appCreate/appUpdate crash on null permissions input `permissions` is an optional input on `AppInput`, but `clean_input` passed the raw value straight to `ensure_app_permissions_allowed`, which crashed with an unhandled `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable` whenever the field was null or omitted (the mutation document still binds `permissions: $permissions`, so an unsupplied variable arrives as `None`). Normalize the popped value with `or []` so a null input means "no permissions". This also closes a latent privilege escalation: `None` would otherwise reach `get_permissions(None)`, which returns *every* permission, silently creating a fully privileged app. `app_install.py` already guarded the same call with `if permissions:` and is unaffected. Adds a parametrized regression test covering both the omitted and the explicit null case. Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com> * Keep appUpdate permissions untouched on null input Follow-up to the previous commit, which normalized a null `permissions` input to `[]` in both mutations. That was wrong for `appUpdate`: it made a null input *clear* the app's existing permissions, so any client sending a partial update without the field would silently strip them. Guard on `is not None` instead. A null input now leaves the key out of `cleaned_input` entirely, so `_save_m2m` skips the relation and the existing permissions survive; an explicit empty list still resolves to an empty queryset and clears them. `appCreate` adopts the same shape for symmetry. Its behavior is unchanged - a null input still creates an app with no permissions - it just no longer runs a pointless `get_permissions([])` query on that path. Note that omitted and explicit-null inputs are indistinguishable here: in graphql-core 2 an unsupplied variable inside an input literal resolves to null, so `input: {}` and `input: {permissions: null}` share one code path. Splits the appUpdate test by behavior: null/omitted keeps the permissions, empty list clears them. Adds the empty-list case to the appCreate test.
